minutes.headline: Commission denied waiver of abutter notice for a water main, approved a septic RDA 5-2 and a Girl Scout bench.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard Girl Scouts propose a recycled-plastic bench, and took up a water district request to waive abutter notification on a long Mass Ave water main project. It handled several RDA and NOI hearings, continued others, discussed how to run RDAs more efficiently, and reviewed upkeep and funding of the Hollis Road house and pollinator habitat. It also closed out certificates of compliance and enforcement orders and declined a land offer on Leominster Road.

what_happened.line: The commission rejected the water district's request to waive abutter notice on a long Mass Ave water main, requiring notice to abutters within the 100-foot buffer zone.
The water district will notify those abutters and return October 19; the hearing will be re-advertised.
The commission approved the 10 Maple Parkway septic RDA 5-2, but a later redo vote on its negative determination was not fully audible.
A negative determination for the 408 Electric Avenue RDA passed 3-2 with one recusal, and the commission approved the Girl Scouts' recycled-plastic bench.
The commission voted to tell the Board of Selectmen it is not interested in the 35 Leominster Road land offer.

why_it_matters: Abutters within 100 feet of the Mass Ave water main route will get formal notice before the commission rules on a project that digs near wetlands.
The Hollis Road house rent and gift fund, and the cost of the window contract, are spending the commission is still reviewing, and they bear on how conservation money is used.
The Leominster Road decision means the commission will not take the offered 17 acres, so that parcel will not come into conservation land through this route.
watch_next: October 19: the water district returns to the commission with abutter notice given and the hearing re-advertised.
November 2: continued hearings for 509 Townsend Harbor Road and 260 Falula Road; officer elections wait until Katie Childs can attend.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on most votes: the bench, the abutter-notification waiver, 127 Chase Road, the 408 Electric Avenue split, the continuances, 160 Mass Ave and the 35 Leominster Road vote. The one substantive difference is the 10 Maple Parkway RDA. Ours has 5-2 and a second "redo" vote with no audible tally, and the official minutes have 4-2 and one vote.
